quarterly_data.signal: ECOC 2026 product demonstration (official press release, not a call): Lumentum announced its plan to demonstrate an eight-wavelength dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) laser module in an External Laser Small Form Factor Pluggable (ELSFP). The module's optical interface is designed to meet the applicable requirements of the Optical Compute Interconnect Multi-Source Agreement (OCI MSA), and it is intended for external laser source applications in co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO) architectures. It provides eight simultaneous DWDM wavelengths across two four-channel bands centered near 1311 nm and 1331 nm; the design targets wavelength accuracy of +/-0.2 nm and demonstrates up to 24 dBm (~250 mW) of optical output power per wavelength at the fiber, with all eight channels operating simultaneously from a single pluggable module at approximately 12 W of power consumption. The module uses Lumentum's Ultra High Power (UHP) laser platform, already in production, in an eight-channel configuration. Lumentum expects initial availability of the DWDM ELSFP module with an OCI MSA optical interface in the first half of calendar year 2027. Sri Venkat (SVP and GM, Components) called CPO and NPO 'defining architectures for AI scale-up' and external laser sources 'a critical building block of that shift', and said the demonstration positions Lumentum to serve customers as the CPO/NPO market scales.
quarterly_data.figure: eight DWDM wavelengths in two four-channel bands near 1311 nm and 1331 nm; wavelength accuracy target +/-0.2 nm; up to 24 dBm (~250 mW) per wavelength at the fiber; approximately 12 W module power; initial availability expected in the first half of calendar year 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Alongside the ELSFP demonstration, Lumentum said it will showcase a scale-across networking display featuring products for high-capacity inter-data-center connectivity at ECOC 2026, and that the Lumentum OCS R300 optical circuit switch will be on exhibit in its booth, highlighting its optical switching portfolio for scalable AI infrastructure. The release gives no OCS specifications, customers or figures.

ECOC 2026 joint demonstration (official press release, not a call): Lumentum announced plans for a joint board-level demonstration with Qualcomm Technologies and Corning of a high-density die-to-die (D2D) optical interconnect for AI scale-up architectures, combining a D2D interface IP subsystem from Qualcomm Technologies with Lumentum's VCSEL-based optical interconnect platform and Corning multimode fiber connectivity. The massively parallel optical D2D architecture is designed for future co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO) implementations supporting emerging D2D interfaces such as UCIe, extending high-density D2D connectivity over multimode-fiber optical links spanning tens of meters while maintaining low latency and power consumption. The proof-of-concept configuration uses optical channels operating at 32 Gb/s NRZ; the architecture is designed to support approximately 1 Tb/s/mm of shoreline bandwidth density today, with line of sight to approximately 4 Tb/s/mm through higher lane rates and increased channel density. This is a proof-of-concept demonstration; the release gives no product availability date, customer or commercial terms.
quarterly_data.figure: 32 Gb/s NRZ optical channels (proof-of-concept); approximately 1 Tb/s/mm shoreline bandwidth density today, line of sight to approximately 4 Tb/s/mm

quarterly_data.signal: The D2D demonstration's optical interconnect uses Lumentum's optical engine based on advanced-packaged 1060 nm VCSEL technology, with approximately 10 Tb/s of aggregate transmit and receive capacity and high-density two-dimensional VCSEL and photodetector arrays with backside lens technology. The platform is built on Lumentum's ultra-high-volume 3D sensing manufacturing base and is designed to support high shoreline bandwidth density, signal integrity and energy-efficient optical connectivity for board-level and system-level AI scale-up architectures. CTO Matt Sysak said the demonstration shows how Lumentum's 1060 nm VCSEL platform can bring high-density optical connectivity closer to AI compute, and described it as showing 'a practical path toward compact, energy-efficient optical D2D links for next-generation AI scale-up architectures'.
quarterly_data.figure: 1060 nm VCSEL optical engine; approximately 10 Tb/s aggregate transmit and receive capacity
